_extraction_flags.notes: Valid Modeling/Analytic Paper. Focuses on the design and optimization of LFM-CPM waveforms for FSO-ISAC.

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Fig 1: System model (Device A: ISAC Tx/Rx, Device B: Comm Rx). Monostatic Sensing (ToF). Fig 2: Min Euclidean Distance vs h. Fig 3: BER vs SNR. Fig 4: RMSE vs SNR. Fig 5: Rate vs SNR with Sensing Constraints.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: FSO-ISAC. Waveform: LFM-CPM (Linear Frequency Modulation - Continuous Phase Modulation). Modified for IM/DD using DC bias and Hilbert transform. Benefits: Constant envelope (before bias), high power efficiency, high spectral efficiency. Trade-off: Comm (BER) vs Sensing (CRB) depends on Modulation Index (h) and Chirp Rate (mu).
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Comm: 100-200 Mbps achievable. Sensing: <10 cm accuracy (RMSE). Trade-off analysis shows h=1.75 good for Comm, h=3.875 good for Sensing.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Solid theoretical analysis. Novel waveform for optical ISAC. Addresses the constant modulus constraint issue for power efficiency.

bibliographic.title: Free Space Optical Integrated Sensing and Communication Based on LFM and CPM
bibliographic.authors: Yunfeng Wen, Fang Yang, Jian Song, Zhu Han

application.scenario_description: FSO-ISAC node (Device A) communicating with Device B while sensing range to Device B (or other targets).

key_contribution.key_contribution: Proposal of LFM-CPM waveform for FSO-ISAC compatible with IM/DD. Optimization of waveform parameters (h, mu) to balance Comm BER and Sensing CRB.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: Lack of constant-envelope waveforms for FSO-ISAC that offer high power efficiency and simultaneous Comm & Sensing capability.

receiver.notes: IM/DD. Hilbert Transform used for envelope recovery.

integration.notes: Simultaneous Comm & Sensing using single waveform.

waveform.notes: Unified LFM-CPM. LFM chirp + CPM data modulation.

comm_metrics.notes: Up to 200 Mbps with M=4. BER depends on SNR and parameter h.

tradeoff.notes: Fig 5 shows Rate vs SNR under Sensing Constraints. Higher sensing precision requirement reduces achievable rate window.
